text:
A: Afternoon! Gary. You alright?
B: Hi, yes, I'm good, thank you. Akosua. Can you hear me okay?
A: Loud and clear. Where are you, Akosua?
B: Thornton Heath, South London. Near Croydon.
A: Croydon, I've been down there for work. Trading estate off the Purley Way. I'm Aldridge, near Walsall. Fixings and fasteners, that's my game. Senior sales. On the road most of the week, keeps me out of trouble.
B: Oh wow, sounds very busy.
A: Fifty-odd hours, but you get used to it. Got a decent car out of it, so I'm not complaining. What about you, what do you do?
B: Erm. To be honest I'm sort of between jobs right now. I was in HR at a housing association, and they did a restructure and I was made redundant. So I'm job hunting. Sorry.
A: No need to say sorry, mate. Happens to the best of us. I've seen it loads in my line. HR though, eh? You'd have been the one sitting me down for the chat about my expenses.
B: Ha! Maybe. I did a lot of those conversations, to be honest. The difficult ones. People always said I was good in the room, it was the paperwork I was bad at.
A: Well, that's the bit that matters, isn't it. The people bit. Paperwork, you get someone else to do it. That's what I do.
B: That's exactly what I did! I had a colleague who kept me on track with deadlines. I miss her more than the job, honestly.
A: There you go. What sort of thing are you after?
B: Something like before. Council, or housing again. Part-time or hybrid, because of my daughter, the school run. She's nine.
A: Makes sense. You'll walk into something, you will. Someone who can talk to people, firms are crying out for that. My daughter's doing business at Nottingham Trent. Final year. First one in our family to go to uni.
B: Oh, you must be so proud.
A: Ah, you know. She's done alright. Doesn't get it from me, mind. Do you get away much? Holidays and that?
B: Erm, I go back to Ghana every couple of years. Family, weddings, funerals mostly. Christmas usually.
A: Ghana, I've never done Africa. I did Dubai for my fiftieth. Got upgraded, beautiful hotel. But that's a long flight, Ghana, is it?
B: About six and a half hours. I hate flying though. I pray the whole way, my mum laughs at me.
A: Ha! Whatever works. I just have a lager and nod off. What's the food like out there?
B: Oh, jollof, plantain, light soup. My mum cooks it here as well. Saturday we have waakye. Sorry, I'm making myself hungry.
A: Sounds better than a Toby carvery. That's my Friday. Or the curry house, and they've just put their prices up again. Two quid on a balti, I said to the bloke, you're having a laugh.
B: Everything's gone up. Plantain in Croydon market is crazy now.
A: Tell me about it. Right, I think that's our time. Lovely chatting, Akosua. Good luck with the job hunt, you'll smash it.
B: Thank you, Gary. That's really kind.
A: Tara, then.
